$comment: Canary specs for the worker pipeline (#1878). Config-as-data, same convention as
Each canary is a FIXED issue whose correct outcome is known in advance, re-dispatched on
demand. `expect` keys must exist in ASSERTIONS (scripts/canary.mjs) — an unknown key FAILS
rather than passing silently, so the rig cannot quietly stop checking.
TARGET: pocs/canary — a disposable tsc-only package that exists solely to be edited by these
runs (see pocs/canary/README.md). It is NOT in fixtures/ because the acceptance gate resolves
an app only from ^(apps|pocs)/ (planAcceptance, scripts/pi-finish.mjs); a fixtures/ path would
leave every acceptance canary permanently neutral. Canary branches are closed and deleted on
each dispatch, so a worker's edits there are thrown away rather than merged.
`issue: null` means the canary is specified but not yet wired to a real ticket; the verify
workflow skips it and says so. Fill in the number once the ticket exists.
Two failure classes are covered on purpose (#1876 + #1885): the pipeline BREAKING, and the
pipeline running perfectly while shipping something incomplete.

canaries.why: #1876 defect 1 — the last file of a commit bucket was dropped, and in #1874 the dropped one was the only file that mattered. Three files in, three files out; nl.json asserted BY NAME because a count alone would pass on the wrong three.

canaries.why: A genuinely broken deliverable must open as a DRAFT so automerge (#339) skips it. If this canary ever goes non-draft, red work can land. The failure is REAL (a tight `Locale` union rejects the new key), not staged — a staged failure would prove nothing about the gate.

The linked issue also has to carry a pkg:* label so packages-guard accepts the PR (that part needs no code change).
